newsitem.title: USA: Clinton seeks legal, ethical review of cloning.
newsitem.headline: Clinton seeks legal, ethical review of cloning.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Monday asked an expert bioethics panel to review legal and ethical ramifications of cloning, spurred by reports of a cloned sheep in Scotland, the White House said.

Clinton asked the National Bioethics Advisory Panel, which was appointed last year, to examine the issue of cloning with special regard to any applications with humans, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said at a briefing.

"The White House has asked the advisory commission to review that to make a judgment as to whether we really need to focus more clearly on the dimension of this scientific and technological development that might pertain to any activity involving human beings," McCurry said.

He said Clinton signed an executive order in 1995 banning federal funding for creation of human embryos for research purposes, and noted that the commission could look at whether private researchers "have to be sensitive to these issues."

Calling the cloning issue "a very troubling subject," McCurry said the inquiry had been sparked by "the very startling news from Scotland." He said the panel might be asked to report back within 90 days.

Last weekend, Ian Wilmut of the Roslin Institute near Edinburgh reported that he had used the cell of an adult sheep to create a baby clone. Wilmut has stressed he intends to use the technique on animals, not people.
